title: Pluperfect + tenses
subtitle: had/was + participle: what happened before another past moment

explain.text: The **pluperfect** (*voltooid verleden tijd*) tells you about something that was already finished **before another moment in the past**. You build it like the perfect, but the auxiliary is in the past: **had / hadden** or **was / waren**, plus the participle at the end.
The choice between *hebben* and *zijn* is **the same as in the perfect**: *zijn* for verbs of change of place or state (*gaan, komen, vertrekken, worden*), *hebben* for the rest.

explain.nl: Toen ik aankwam, was de trein al vertrokken.
explain.en: When I arrived, the train had already left.

explain.nl: Ik had mijn sleutels vergeten, dus ik kon niet naar binnen.
explain.en: I had forgotten my keys, so I could not get in.

explain.text: Only use the pluperfect when there is a second, later moment in the past. For one single past event, use the simple past or the perfect.

items.q: Toen ik op het station aankwam, ___ de trein al vertrokken.

explain.text: In a story you usually tell the main events in the **simple past**, and you go one step back with the **pluperfect**. Words like **nadat** (after), **voordat** (before), **toen** (when), **al** (already), **nog niet** (not yet), **inmiddels** (by then) and **daarvoor** (before that) help the listener to place the events.

head: word
meaning
example
rows: Nadat ik had gegeten, ging ik naar bed.

explain.text: In a subordinate clause the verbs go to the end. With the pluperfect both orders are correct: *Nadat ik **had gegeten**, …* and *Nadat ik **gegeten had**, …*.

explain.nl: Nadat zij de brief had gelezen, belde zij haar zus.
explain.en: After she had read the letter, she called her sister.

explain.nl: Ik had nog niet gegeten, toen hij belde.
explain.en: I had not eaten yet when he called.

explain.text: The event with **had/was + participle** happened first. The event in the simple past (*belde, kwam, ging*) happened later.

explain.text: Three past tenses, three jobs. The **perfect** reports a finished fact with a link to now. The **simple past** tells a story or describes a situation. The **pluperfect** looks back from a past moment to something that happened before it.

head: tense
use
example
rows: Ik stond op, at en ging weg.
Toen ik vertrok, had ik al gegeten.

explain.text: The pluperfect is also the tense for **reasons and background** in a past story: *Zij was boos, omdat hij niet had gebeld.* And with **nog nooit** (never before): *Ik had nog nooit sneeuw gezien.*

explain.nl: Toen ik wakker werd, had het gesneeuwd.
explain.en: When I woke up, it had snowed.

explain.nl: Ik had nog nooit sneeuw gezien.
explain.en: I had never seen snow before.

explain.text: *Ik had gisteren gewerkt* sounds unfinished: the listener waits for "…toen er iets gebeurde". With only one past event, use *Ik heb gisteren gewerkt* or *Ik werkte gisteren*.

items.q: Which sentence is natural? (one finished event yesterday)
items.explain: One past event: perfect. Werken takes hebben, and had needs a second past moment.
